body.p: Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration of the present application in view of the
foregoing amendments and the reasons that follow.
Claims 1, 3, 5, 10, and 12 have been amended. Claims 21-28 are new. Claims 13-20 have
been canceled. No new matter has been added. These amendments are made without prejudice or
disclaimer.
Support for the amendments can be found throughout the Application, for example, in the
Specification in paragraphs [0054]-[0058] and [0061] and in FIGS. 3B-4 and 6-7E.
Support for new claims 21-23 can be found throughout the Application, for example, in the
Specification in paragraphs [0070]-[0075] and in FIGS. 3B-4.
Support for new claim 24 can be found throughout the Application, for example, in the
Specification in paragraph [0075] and in FIG. 4.
Support for new claims 25-27 can be found throughout the Application, for example, in the
Specification in paragraphs [0079]-[0084] and in FIGS. 7A-7E.
Support for new claim 28 can be found throughout the Application, for example, in the
Specification in paragraph [0055] and in FIGS. 3B-4 and 6-7E.
After amending the claims as set forth above, claims 1-12 and 21-28 remain pending in
this application, with claims 10 and 11 being withdrawn. Applicant respectfully requests
reconsideration of these claims.
Claims 1-3, 5, and 6 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 102(a)(1) as allegedly being
anticipated by EP 2357356 ("Katz"). Applicant respectfully traverses these rejections.
Amended claim 1 recites in part and with emphasis added:

1. A tunable mass damper assembly attachable to a rotor blade configured to rotate about a rotor axis, the tunable mass damper assembly comprising: a base configured to be attached to the rotor blade; and
a pendulum mass structure comprising: a first end rotatably coupled to the base about a pivot axis substantially perpendicular to a plane containing the rotor axis; and
a second end configured to rotate freely about the pivot axis in accordance with a rotational speed of the rotor blade about the rotor axis,

the pendulum mass structure being configured to reduce vibratory forces of the rotor blade induced by a rotation of the rotor blade about the rotor axis, and an entirety of the pendulum mass structure being configured to be contained within and enclosed by the rotor blade.
Katz does not anticipate the subject matter of the pending claims, because it does not satisfy
the requirements that "a prior art reference must disclose all elements of the claim within the four corners of the document, and it must disclose those elements arranged as in the claim." See
Microsoft Corp. v. Biscotti, Inc., 878 F.3d 1052, 1068 (Fed. Cir. 2017).
Katz does not disclose every element of claim 1. For example, Katz does not disclose
tunable mass damper assembly including a pendulum mass structure with a "second end configured to rotate freely about the pivot axis in accordance with a rotational speed of the rotor
blade about the rotor axis," as recited in amended claim 1.
The Office Action indicates on page 3 that Katz discloses a "mass actuator 4" including a
"mass 6" and an "arm 25" that are allegedly equivalent to the pendulum mass structure of claim 1.

However, the mass 6 and arm 26 do not include a "second end configured to rotate freely about [a] pivot axis." As recited in amended claim 1. The lever arm 25 is "connected to the rotor blade 1 via an integral joint 26." (Katz Translation [0055]). The mass actuator 4 of Katz further includes an "actuator 5" that is "designed as a linear drive which drives the mass [6] directly."
Accordingly, the mass actuator 4 of Katz does not include a "second end configured to rotate freely about the pivot axis," but instead includes a first end coupled to the joint 26 and a second end
coupled to and driven by the actuator 5.
For at least these reasons, claim 1 is allowable over Katz.
Claims 2, 3, 5, and 6 depend from claim 1 and are allowable for at least the same reasons
as claim 1, even without regard to the further patentable features recited therein.
Accordingly, Applicant respectfully requests withdrawal of the rejections under
Claim 4 was rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Katz in
view of U.S. Patent No. 5,639,214 ("Guimbal"). Claims 7-9 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103
as allegedly being unpatentable over Katz.
Claims 4 and 7-9 depend from claim 1. Guimbal fails to remedy the deficiencies of Katz
discussed above with respect to claim 1. Thus claim 1 and its dependent claims, claims 4 and 7- 9, are patentable over the combination of Katz and Guimbal.
Accordingly, Applicant respectfully requests withdrawal of the rejections under
Claims 21-29 depend from claim 1 and are allowable for at least the same reasons as claim
1, even without regard to the further patentable features recited therein.
Further, the cited references fail to disclose, teach, or suggest "a center block, wherein the
base and the pendulum mass structure are positioned within the center block," as recited in claim 21. For at least this additional reason, claim 21 and claims 22 and 23, which depend therefrom,
are allowable over the cited references.
The cited references fail to disclose, teach, or suggest a tunable mass damper assembly

including a base "rotatably coupled to the rotor blade," as recited in claim 24. The Office Action alleges that "whichever structure arm 25 and joint 26 are attached to" is equivalent to the base recited in claim 1. However, Katz does not disclose that this alleged structure is "rotatably coupled to the rotor blade." For at least this additional reason, claim 24 is allowable over the cited
references.
The cited references fail to disclose, teach, or suggest a tunable mass damper assembly
including "a first pendulum arm arranged substantially parallel to a second pendulum arm," as recited in claim 25. For at least this additional reason, claim 25 and claims 26 and 27, which
depend therefrom, are allowable over the cited references.
The cited references fail to disclose, teach, or suggest a tunable mass damper assembly
"wherein a first side of the pendulum mass is coupled to the at least one pendulum arm, wherein
a cross-section of the first side is larger than a cross-section of a second side of the pendulum
mass, the second side opposite the first side," as recited in claim 28. For at least this additional
reason, claim 28 is allowable over the cited references.
For at least the reasons discussed above, Applicant respectfully requests allowance of the
new claims.
To the extent a requirement for restriction and/or election of species was made final in
this application, Applicant asserts that all pending claims other than those identified as
withdrawn, are either generic or read on the elected invention and/or species. Applicant intends
for this Reply to be fully responsive to the outstanding Office Action.
Applicant believes that the application is in condition for allowance. Favorable
reconsideration is respectfully requested. The Examiner is invited to contact the undersigned by
telephone if it is felt that a telephone interview would advance prosecution.
The Commissioner is hereby authorized to charge any additional fees which may be
required for this application to Deposit Account No. 19-0741. If any extensions of time are
needed for timely acceptance of papers submitted herewith, Applicant hereby petitions for such extensions under 37 CFR § 1.136 and authorizes payment of any such extension fees to Deposit
Account No. 19-0741.
Respectfully submitted,
